analysis_notes.series_context: Part of a shared universe ('IFverse'): the gray-coat woman, Jay (teleporter, 'blinks'), the gravity kid, the kid who can't break, the boy who stops time, the power-copying brother, the 'gym where everyone floated' all recur from earlier What IF episodes. Description cross-links 'What IF You Could Copy Powers?'. Each episode is a standalone origin story that lands inside the ongoing arc.
analysis_notes.description_cta: Description repeats the question hooks: 'Would you ever turn back into yourself?' and 'Is the woman in the gray coat telling the truth? Drop it in the comments.'

title_pattern.template: What IF You Could [Verb a Superpower]?
title_pattern.notes: Channel-wide fixed template (IFOLOGY brand bakes 'IF' in caps into the title). Second person, one power, no numbers, no qualifiers, 5 words. The power is a single verb everyone already understands (shapeshift / copy powers / teleport / stop time), so the click is pure wish-fulfilment plus 'but what's the catch'. Tags farm sibling queries ('what if you could turn into anyone', 'change your appearance'). Payoff is not an explainer: it is a second-person life story from age 6 to 12+ that ends inside the channel's ongoing superhero arc.

thumbnail.composition: Single giant head-and-shoulders bust centred, filling ~90% of frame height, cropped at the hoodie. Face split vertically down the middle: left half is the channel's black-blob stickman head (glossy black, sly half-lidded eye, big white smirk), right half is a realistic-ish painted human face (ginger hair, stubble, wide worried blue eye). Seam is a wavy liquid/ink drip edge glowing cyan-violet.
thumbnail.text: None. No words, no arrows, no logo.
thumbnail.colours: Deep violet/indigo night city skyline background (blurred, low contrast); saturated royal-blue hoodie; warm orange skin and hair on the right half vs pure black on the left; cyan + magenta glow along the split seam. Basically complementary orange/blue with a neon accent.
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: No scale contrast; the contrast is identity/style contrast: cartoon vs human, black vs warm skin, smug vs scared expression on the same face. Extreme close-up so it reads at phone size.
thumbnail.why_it_works: Visualises the title's power in one image with no text needed (half-transformed face = mid-shapeshift). Two opposing expressions on one face create an instant question (which one is the real you?). Big face + eye contact is the highest-CTR thumbnail archetype; the stickman half keeps channel branding recognisable; the glowing seam is the only high-frequency detail and leads the eye to the centre. Note: thumbnail is a painted, more detailed illustration than the in-video 3D style.

hook.verbatim_0_to_5s: There are two of your mom in the kitchen. One of them is making pancakes. The other one is standing by the fridge holding a spatula smiling way too hard.
hook.verbatim_5_to_35s: The second one is you. Your dad walks in, looks at the first mom, looks at the second mom, and very slowly puts his coffee down. / DAD: Okay, I need both of you to say something only your mom would know. / The real mom crosses her arms. You open your mouth to answer and out comes the voice of a 7-year-old boy. / YOU (as mom): I'm your wife. / The dog starts barking. Only at you. / DAD: Go to your room and give me back my face.
hook.title_drop: 35.6 s: 'So, what if you could shapeshift? What if you could become anyone or anything just by thinking about it? Here's how it works.' with an on-screen serif title card 'WHAT IF YOU COULD SHAPESHIFT?' over a glowing mid-transform figure.
devices: Cold open in medias res: a funny, concrete, domestic scene that already shows the power working AND failing (the payoff of the 'catch')
Second-person 'you' from word one; the viewer is the impostor
Visual paradox in the first line ('two of your mom') = instant curiosity gap, resolved at 8.7 s ('The second one is you')
Comedic button with voiced dialogue ('give me back my face') before the title drop

The hook scene foreshadows the climax: two identical women face each other on the stadium stairs at 16:21 ('which one of you is the real one?'), so the cold open is a structural rhyme, not a throwaway gag
Plants the voice limitation (kid voice) that pays off at 16:07 ('in her voice, perfectly, for the first time in your life')

beats.summary: Two moms in the kitchen; the second is you. Dad tests both, you answer in a 7-year-old's voice, dog barks only at you, dad: 'give me back my face'. Comedy + shows power and its flaws.
'So, what if you could shapeshift?...Here's how it works.' Serif title card over glowing transforming figure.
Real-world anchor: cuttlefish change colour/pattern in under a second, and are thought to be colourblind. Two quick 'weird part' facts.
How YOUR version works: bones slide, face folds, hair grows/retracts, ~3 s, 'feels like stretching'. Skeleton line-drawing insert.
University of York: average person knows ~5,000 faces; brain has a face area; 'the whole world is basically a costume store'.
Age ~6, hide-and-seek: you wish to be a laundry basket and become one; can't stand up (no legs, a lid); mom drops socks on you; you pop back and mom screams. Mom: 'Nobody panic'.
Mom makes you practise nightly: 'Basket, boy, basket, boy.'

Rule 1 keep your weight (50 kg house cat breaks couch). Rule 2 only become what you've studied (teacher perfect from front, your hair and dinosaur backpack from behind). Rule 3 look like, not become (pro baller's body, your jump shot). Voice is hardest; kid voice for years.

Payoff of wish-fulfilment: never lose hide-and-seek (coat rack, plant, Christmas tree with ornament on nose), forge permission slip as mom (handwriting fails), become principal and cancel homework then meet the real principal and turn into a water fountain that runs away, 50 kg penguin at the zoo.
Best friend Milo, who talks to animals (crow finds lost keys). Mutual secret. Short dialogue exchange: 'Dude, you can talk to birds.'

Problem 1 weight: 50 kg mouse/pigeon can't fly. Problem 2 dogs: 300M vs 6M smell sensors, dogs know it's you. Problem 3 details: fingerprints (dad's phone won't unlock), scars, tells. Problem 4 at 12, after 3 weeks as a lifeguard you can't remember your own face; mom: 'That's not your chin'; you carry a photo of yourself. 'Rule four, don't forget your own face.'

Milo goes viral as 'bird boy' (pigeon statue, 2M views, news). 3 days later a black van takes him; driver wears gray gloves; you chase on bike; cover story (aunt, transferred); pigeons wait. Vow: 'Somebody knows where he is, and I'm going to find them.'

A year as a hundred people (mail carrier, police desk, old man feeding pigeons). Hear of the gym where everyone floated and a woman in a gray coat with a gray van. Gray coat + van + gloves. Find the van behind a car wash: a garage with a team.
They have a mind reader, so you enter as an object nobody looks at: a big gray equipment case on wheels next to the snack shelf. You stay a month.

Observational montage of the team (red cap arm-wrestles beetle suit, goggles girl sleeps floating, Jay blinks in for granola daily and ties his shoe on you, peanut butter bar gag). Near-discovery: headphones mind reader senses someone thinking about Milo; you stop thinking for 3 hours. 'They're actually nice. That's the worst part.'

Gray-coat woman returns alone, no gloves, makes a guilty phone call ('I'll bring them when it's time'). You become a hand on wheels, pick the drawer lock: folders on every kid with how to stop them; at the bottom Milo's school photo stamped FOUND in red.

Phones buzz: 'The stadium. Both of them.' Championship game, 70,000 people; the boy who stops time + the power-copying brother. Team grabs the case ('weighs like a whole person' / 'probably the snacks'). Van ride: team nerves dialogue; you see her hands are bare on the wheel.

Stadium already frozen: spiral football hanging, fireworks paused like flowers. Team freezes too; only the gray-coat woman walks. Hooded boy holds time on the 50-yard line; man in black coat touches people in the crowd. She cuffs the boy to the goalpost; time crashes back.

Team combo: webs pin hands, gravity kid drops the floating man, goggles girl lands, red cap + beetle man hold arms, kid who can't break sits on him, Jay: 'Hi. Remember me?' Sister/brother reveal: 'Hello again, sister.' 'It's over.'

The case opens its lid. You stand up, become the gray-coat woman (perfect voice for the first time), order 'Let him go'. Two of her on the stairs ('which one is the real one?' rhymes with the cold open). Brother escapes, steals red cap's strength; you turn your hand into her key and free the hooded boy: 'Somebody who needs a favor.'

Rapid escalation, each team power countered by a form: become Jay (two Jays, web confusion, you go rubbery), goalpost (flier bounces off), pile of jerseys then tiger mascot, mind reader outs you, gravity kid crushes you so you become a flat tarp (physics reasoning: tall things snap, flat things spread weight).

Real sister catches brother at the tunnel; time stops again; both can move. He gently removes her hand ('You're still my brother'). He kneels by the tarp: knows you opened the cuff, knows you're looking for the bird boy. 'The black vans, the gray gloves. You want to know who drives them? ... Ask her.' Exits with the hooded boy.

You turn back into yourself with the photo in your pocket; team circles you; comic beat ('I've been your case for a month' / 'I carried you to the van like nine times'). Nobody laughs. You confront her about Milo and the black vans; her face closes. She just takes out her keys: 'Everybody in the van. You, too.' She looks at none of them.

'So, what would you do if you could shapeshift? Would you hide as a case...or walk in as yourself? And is the woman in the gray coat telling the truth? Tell us in the comments because this is only the beginning.' Captions on screen, then IFOLOGY logo/subscribe end card over the van leaving the stadium.

pacing.wpm_note: Fast but clear narrator delivery (~3.2 words/s), with ~30 short voiced character lines (multiple voices) inserted between narration; essentially no pauses except the frozen-stadium beat and the final confrontation.
pacing.shot_length_note: Explainer/rules section (0-7 min) cuts every ~3.5 s (every gag gets its own shot); story/drama sections slow to 5-9 s shots with slow push-ins; quieter emotional beats (19:00-20:00) as long as 15 s. Camera almost always has a gentle push or drift.
pacing.re_hook_interval_s: ~30-60 s: numbered RULE/PROBLEM cards in the first half, then mystery reveals (gray gloves 8:00, FOUND 11:24, bare hands 12:52, 'Ask her' 20:11) in the second half.

techniques_worth_copying: Hybrid format: first ~7 minutes are a 'what if' explainer (science fact, mechanic, numbered rules, numbered problems) told as a second-person childhood; the remaining 15 minutes turn into a serialized superhero story. Searchers get the premise; retention comes from story.
Cold open is a scene from later in the life (age ~7) that shows power + flaw + comedy in 35 s, then title drop with 'Here's how it works'.

Every rule and problem is immediately demonstrated with a concrete visual gag (50 kg cat breaks couch; teacher perfect from the front, kid from behind; dad's phone refuses fingerprint). Rules are numbered on screen as mini-chapters.

Rules are set up so the climax can use them: weight rule -> goalpost the flier bounces off and the flat tarp vs gravity; 'only what you've studied' -> watching the woman for 30 days; voice is hardest -> first perfect voice in the climax; 'don't forget your own face' -> photo in pocket. Setup/payoff density is very high.
One real stat per explainer beat with a named source (University of York 5,000 faces; 300M vs 6M dog smell sensors; cuttlefish colourblind) gives credibility to a fantasy.
Sidekick with a complementary power (Milo talks to animals) creates emotional stakes; his abduction is the inciting incident at ~30%.
Clue triad repeated for memory: 'A gray coat, a gray van, and gray gloves'; recurring object motifs (gloves, keys, peanut-butter granola bars, the case).

Protagonist hides in plain sight as an object (case with only eyes visible) for half the video: dramatic irony every time a character leans on or lifts it ('weighs like a whole person' / 'probably the snacks').
Climax rhymes with the cold open (two identical people, 'which one is the real one?').
Short voiced dialogue lines (different voices) punctuate narration every 20-60 s; they carry jokes and emotional turns.

Ends on an unresolved moral question about a recurring character + two comment prompts ('hide as a case or walk in as yourself?', 'is she telling the truth?'), shown as on-screen captions; 'this is only the beginning' promises a sequel. Description repeats the comment prompts.
Shared universe: recurring team from other episodes makes each video a door into the back catalogue (description link to 'What IF You Could Copy Powers?').
Consistent transformation VFX language: cyan holographic body + white sparkle particles every time the power is used, so the viewer instantly reads 'power happening'.
Mid-roll subscribe lower-third at ~2:02 right after the first big gag lands.

code_only_remake_needs.feasibility: Medium-hard. The source is a 3D low-poly render (Blender-like) with soft lighting, vignette, letterbox and depth of field. A code-only remake should translate it into 2.5D: flat SVG sets with parallax layers, and the channel-style characters as SVG rigs. The character design is the easy part (black circle head, two white dot/arc eyes, white mouth arc, rim-light crescent, simple body + clothing colour).
code_only_remake_needs.character_rig: SVG stickman/bean rig: black circle head with a cream rim-light crescent, expression set (smile, smirk, shock 'o', worried, half-lid suspicious, crying), accessory slots (caps, visor, goggles, headphones, hair tufts, glasses), coloured hoodie/cardigan body with simple limb bones for walk/point/arms-out/crouch. Needs ~12 recurring characters distinguished only by hat/hair + clothing colour.
code_only_remake_needs.transformation_fx: Reusable <ShapeshiftFX>: cross-fade between two SVG silhouettes via a cyan-to-white gradient overlay, scanline/hologram shimmer, sparkle particle burst (20-40 white diamonds), 0.6-1 s. Also morph-target shapes for object forms (basket, case, tarp, goalpost, tree) with two blinking eyes overlay.
code_only_remake_needs.sets: ~15 flat sets: kitchen, hallway with stairs, living room, classroom with chalkboard, school corridor with lockers, basketball court, park with city skyline, reef (underwater), snowy penguin pen, suburban street (day and dusk purple), garage HQ with string lights and shelves, night stadium (crowd as repeated tiny blob sprites in rows, field lines, goalposts, floodlights), tunnel. Each with 3 parallax layers and a lighting/vignette overlay.
code_only_remake_needs.graphics: Flat white-line-on-black inserts (skeleton, brain with face icons, fingerprint, frozen fireworks); numbered section cards (RULE 1-4, PROBLEM 1-4) as small top-left uppercase labels; numeric callouts ('YOU = 50 KG', '300,000,000', '70,000 PEOPLE'); dossier folder with red 'FOUND' handwritten stamp; phone message UI; TV news lower third 'BIRD BOY'; serif title card.
code_only_remake_needs.camera: Virtual camera with constant slow push-in/drift (scale 1.0->1.08 over a shot), occasional lateral truck and top-down; shot/reverse two-shots; ECU on faces for reactions. Letterbox bars + radial vignette + subtle film grain.
code_only_remake_needs.audio: Narrator TTS at ~190 wpm (Kokoro) plus 4-6 distinct character voices for short dialogue lines; music bed shifting from playful to tense; SFX for transforms (whoosh+chime), barks, crowd, fireworks.
code_only_remake_needs.timeline: Storyboard of ~280 shots for 22 min (avg 4.8 s); first 7 min at ~3.5 s/shot. For our pilots, a 8-12 min version with the same hybrid shape (explainer rules first, then story that uses every rule) is more realistic.
code_only_remake_needs.hard_parts: Crowd scenes (instancing hundreds of sprites cheaply), action choreography in the climax (webs, gravity, fliers) and readable depth without 3D lighting. Consider Remotion + @remotion/three only if a 3D look is required; otherwise lean into flat 2D.
